text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov welcomes Gulf investors. Stoyanov on Monday starts an official three-day visit to Kuwait.
- Study puts cost of electricity linkage between Gulf Arab states at $1.92 billion.
- Trade declines at the Kuwait Stock Exchange as investors anticipate bi-annual results of listed firms.
- Egyptian manpower companies plan tour of Gulf Arab states to explore employment prospects in the region.

- Kuwait Democratic Forum, a liberal political grouping, holds rally in support of opposition parliamentarian Abdullah al-Naibari who survived a June 6 assassination attempt. Naibari left to Boston on Sunday for further medical treatment.
- About $570 million in compensation to victims of the 1990-91 Iraqi occupation of Kuwait to be paid in September, official says.

- National carriers of Jordan and Kuwait could resume direct flights between the two countries in July, informed sources say. Ties between the two Arab states were badly strained after what Kuwait saw as Jordan's sympathy with Iraq during its 1990-91 occupation of the Gulf state.
- Kuwait Stock Exchange's index fell 43.7 points to 2,340.7 on Sunday.
- Official at the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour rules out open-door policy for foreign workers seeking to change their employers.
